archetypes.name: parity-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan explicitly requires symmetric application to both codex+cursor branches in launch-review.sh and to both function+inline copies in collect-agent-results.sh, plus correct positional-arg counts at all callers of the modified external_launcher_append_outer_meta signature — verifying every parity-required location is named is a correctness gap distinct from generic edge analysis.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that the plan explicitly names all four retry sites in collect-agent-results.sh (launch_outer_retry_or_mark, the inline empty-output outer path, launch_cmd_json_retry_or_mark, and the inline empty-output CMD_JSON path) and that every planned change to launch-review.sh is applied symmetrically to both codex and cursor branches. Check whether external_launcher_append_outer_meta has any callers in the in-scope files beyond the two call sites the plan names (~line 594 codex, ~line 1010 cursor), and flag any caller that would receive the wrong positional-arg count after the 6th-arg extension. Also verify that passing an empty 5th risk arg to preserve the 'high' default is consistent with the function's actual default logic as currently described in lib-external-launcher-common.md. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: shell-portability
archetypes.rationale: The codebase enforces Bash 3.2 compatibility via make lint-bash32 and has specific set-e guard rules for conditional writes in scripts; the plan introduces new array build-and-expand idioms and conditional printf forms whose portability must be verified before implementation.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit each new code pattern described in the plan against the codebase's Bash 3.2 portability rules and set-e conventions documented in BASH_AUTHORING.md. Check that the _outer_sink_args array build-and-expand idiom and the _RUN_EXTERNAL_SINK_ARGS pattern are Bash 3.2 compatible; verify the plan's if-form vs &&-form distinction for conditional writes matches the set-e status of each target script (run-external-agent.sh runs under set -e and must use if-form; lib-external-launcher-common.sh is sourced without set -e and may use &&-form). Flag any proposed pattern that would fail make lint-bash32 or violate the set-e guard rule described in the plan. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: meta-grammar-contract
archetypes.rationale: The .meta file is a shared line-oriented contract between multiple writers and the collect-agent-results.sh parser; adding STDERR_SINK as a new field touches every layer of that contract, and verifying that all write paths, parse sites, reset lists, and doc-update sections are mutually consistent is a boundary/contract concern not fully addressed by generic arch or correctness review.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check that the plan's STDERR_SINK field addition is consistent across all write paths and parse sites: both parse sites in collect-agent-results.sh must update the META_STDERR_SINK reset alongside existing META_* variable resets, and both must include the new case arm. Confirm the validation split is coherent and consistently described across all four doc-update sections: validate_meta_scalar_path in launch-review.sh and run-external-agent.sh reject newline/CR but not '..', while only collect-agent-results.sh's validate_retry_stderr_sink_or_mark rejects '..'. Flag any doc section (run-external-agent.md, lib-external-launcher-common.md, collect-agent-results.md, launch-review.md) that omits or mischaracterizes a validation layer or fails to document the conditional-write (only when non-empty) contract. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
